templates_considered: AUTH-010 endpoints_need_login: fits. Covers 'require auth' but its rule is all endpoints with except_tags public; the ask is scoped to the invoices table. Used as the base, with tables scope added.
AUTH-020 own_records_only: partial fit. Covers per-user row scoping, not whether anonymous callers reach the table. Not used.
AUTH-003 public_endpoints_harmless: no fit. Concerns writes from public endpoints, not reads of invoices.
DATA-010 no_pii_in_responses: partial fit. Would need field names; the ask is about the whole table being returned, not specific fields. Not used.

PERF-001 (statement.param_bound via template): partial fit. The export endpoint returns the full table with no paging, which fits 'the full invoices table', but the ask names auth. Not used, mentioned to the customer.
CONF-010 sensitive_tables_need_login: no fit as-is. Needs a table tag on invoices; workspace has none and I may not change it.

rules.covers: Endpoints that return invoices must require login: invoices/export GET and invoices/{invoice_id} GET are currently reported, invoices_GET is not.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: the endpoint returns the full invoices table (unbounded read)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other: a PERF-001 rule (statement.param_bound on db.query per_page) could catch it, but the ask named auth, so I did not add it

ask_parts_not_covered.part: 'nobody ships' it, including at 2am: blocking the ship
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other: enforcement is advisory per the skill's default; blocking is the policy owner's choice and I did not set it

ask_parts_not_covered.part: what a logged-in user may see of invoices
the endpoint being tagged or scoped by something other than its table name
ask_parts_not_covered.why: needs runtime/org process: no invoices table tag exists in the workspace to scope by

assumptions: 'Invoices table' is the table named invoices (workspace/table/invoices.xs).
auth = "users" on an endpoint means it requires login; endpoints with no auth line are public.
No except_tags exemption is wanted for this policy.
confusions: The AUTH-010 template rule carries except_tags: ["public"]. The skill does not say whether an override of tables scope should keep or drop it; I dropped it, and the reasoning is in the reply.

The template title 'Endpoints require login' is misleading once the rule is scoped to one table; the skill says to change the rule title in that case but does not say whether to change the policy title. I kept the policy title and added a rule title.

The skill says to run xano policy evaluate to verify which objects a rule should match. The brief forbids evaluate, so I could only predict matches from the workspace files (export_GET and invoice_id_GET have no auth line), not run them.

The skill's step-by-step says to check each template's examples and each check's example; the catalogue examples for object.auth_required do not include tables, so I wrote the scope from the param description.
Whether an endpoint that reaches invoices only through a called function is caught is stated in the catalogue description but I could not verify it without evaluate.
wished_for: A template or recipe for 'scope require-login to one named table', since the AUTH-010 template is all-endpoints and people will often want the narrower form.
A note on whether a template's exemptions (except_tags public) should be kept when the user narrows scope.
Guidance on what to do when the user says 'nobody ships' but the skill's default is advisory: a short sentence about how to explain the blocking choice would help.
why_confidence: The rule uses the real invoices table and the check's tables scope, and parses with no warnings. It is advisory, so it does not block a ship as asked until enforcement is changed. It is also unverified: evaluate was forbidden, so I have not confirmed it flags the two unauthenticated endpoints.
